scenes.tts: Chapter one established a rapid route from a gut sensor cell to the vagus. How can that route teach sugar preference when sweet taste is absent?
scenes.visual: HOOK AND CARRIED WORLD, 16:9. Reuse Chapter 1 colour map: gut sensor cell GOLD; vagal neuron BLUE; glutamate TEAL; diffuse hormone GREY; unidentified items WHITE; active or restored GREEN; blocked or silenced RED. In this chapter, fat is WHITE. Show the same gut cross-section at bottom, connected by the BLUE vagus to a simple mouse silhouette at centre. Above, a tongue route enters the mouse from two bottles: sugar and calorie-free sweetener. The gut route ends in a large question mark. Activity pulses continuously along both routes.
scenes.narration: Chapter one established a rapid route from a gut sensor cell to the vagus. How can that route teach sugar preference when sweet taste is absent?

scenes.visual: Title 'How the Gut Teaches Preference' writes above the mouse for 2 seconds. The tongue and gut routes continue pulsing behind it, then the title clears.

scenes.tts: First separate two measurements. Initial attraction is what the mouse chooses at the first sip. Learned preference is how that choice shifts after signals arrive from the gut.
scenes.visual: A horizontal time strip grows beneath the mouse from 'first sip' to 'later choice'. At the left, two lick counters labelled 'schematic' rise equally. At the right, empty preference bars wait. The tongue route is labelled 'initial attraction'; the GOLD-cell-to-BLUE-vagus route is labelled 'post-ingestive learning'.
scenes.narration: First separate two measurements. Initial attraction is what the mouse chooses at the first sip. Learned preference is how that choice shifts after signals arrive from the gut.

scenes.tts: Researchers matched sugar and a calorie-free sweetener for early attraction. Naive mice initially drank at similar rates. Then the sugar bar rose over the choice period.
scenes.visual: At 'early attraction', the two first-sip counters climb together to equal height. A clock hand sweeps across the time strip. Only the later sugar preference bar grows upward in GOLD while the sweetener bar stays low. Label the bars 'schematic time course'.
scenes.narration: Researchers matched sugar and a calorie-free sweetener for early attraction. Naive mice initially drank at similar rates. Then the sugar bar rose over the choice period.

scenes.tts: Suppose sweet taste alone creates that later preference. What should happen in mice that cannot signal sweetness during the choice period?
scenes.visual: The tongue route turns RED and receives a clear cross, while the gut route remains neutral. The later preference bars reset to outlines. Large question: 'No sweet-taste signal: does sugar preference develop?'
scenes.narration: Suppose sweet taste alone creates that later preference. What should happen in mice that cannot signal sweetness during the choice period?

scenes.visual: Deliberate predict pause. Keep the question and empty bars. The gut lumen nutrient dots drift, the BLUE vagus gently pulses and the clock ticks once each second.

scenes.tts: It still develops. Mice lacking the sweet receptor or a taste-transduction channel still preferred sugar later. In mice, learned sugar preference can develop without sweet-taste signalling.
scenes.visual: Keep the tongue route crossed RED. The later sugar bar now grows strongly GOLD and receives a GREEN check. A pulse travels from luminal sugar through the GOLD gut cell and along the BLUE vagus. The sentence 'taste not required for learned preference' appears above the time strip.
scenes.narration: It still develops. Mice lacking the sweet receptor or a taste-transduction channel still preferred sugar later. In mice, learned sugar preference can develop without sweet-taste signalling.

scenes.tts: In Tan and colleagues' assay, gut-delivered sugar activates vagal neurons that acesulfame K does not. Blocking sodium glucose transporter one sharply reduces glucose responses. Intestinal sodium glucose transporter one function is needed for this gut sugar signal.
scenes.caption: In Tan and colleagues' assay, gut-delivered sugar activates vagal neurons that acesulfame K does not. Blocking SGLT1 sharply reduces glucose responses. Intestinal SGLT1 function is needed for this gut sugar signal.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the carried gut world. GOLD sugar dots enter the GOLD sensor cell through a labelled block 'SGLT1', and a BLUE ganglion-response gauge rises. GREY acesulfame K dots leave that gauge unchanged. A RED block covers SGLT1; the glucose gauge falls sharply. Mark both response curves 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: In Tan and colleagues' assay, gut-delivered sugar activates vagal neurons that acesulfame K does not. Blocking SGLT1 sharply reduces glucose responses. Intestinal SGLT1 function is needed for this gut sugar signal.

scenes.tts: Silencing sugar-activated brainstem neurons prevents the learned preference but leaves initial attraction. Activating another population can create preference for a previously less-preferred stimulus.
scenes.visual: Pull back to mouse and time strip. A small brainstem node on the BLUE route turns RED; the later sugar bar collapses while the equal first-sip counters stay unchanged. Then a different brainstem node turns GREEN and a previously low neutral-stimulus bar grows.
scenes.narration: Silencing sugar-activated brainstem neurons prevents the learned preference but leaves initial attraction. Activating another population can create preference for a previously less-preferred stimulus.

scenes.tts: A later experiment targeted C C K labelled duodenal sensor cells. Silencing them strongly reduced the preference advantage above chance. Initial attraction and learned preference are different measurements.
scenes.caption: A later experiment targeted CCK-labelled duodenal sensor cells. Silencing them strongly reduced the preference advantage above chance. Initial attraction and learned preference are different measurements.
scenes.visual: Return to the GOLD sensor cell and add label 'CCK-labelled'. At right, show computed bars from the lesson: control advantage above chance 40.8 points; silenced advantage 8.9 points. A RED light dims the cell and the second bar contracts. Label the chart 'computed from reported preferences'. Keep the first-sip counters unchanged above it.
scenes.narration: A later experiment targeted CCK-labelled duodenal sensor cells. Silencing them strongly reduced the preference advantage above chance. Initial attraction and learned preference are different measurements.

scenes.tts: Sugar is not the only nutrient lesson. Fat preference survives loss of fat taste. Imaging then reveals broad nutrient responders and a distinct fat-only vagal population. The broad population also answers sugar and amino acids, so fat is not carried only by fat-only cells.
scenes.visual: The gut lumen splits into GOLD sugar dots and round WHITE fat droplets, both labelled as cartoons, not molecular structures. The BLUE vagus divides into two distinct branches: one responds to sugar, fat and amino-acid labels; the other lights only for fat and gains label 'fat-only'. Do not encode relative population size in the branch widths.
scenes.narration: Sugar is not the only nutrient lesson. Fat preference survives loss of fat taste. Imaging then reveals broad nutrient responders and a distinct fat-only vagal population. The broad population also answers sugar and amino acids, so fat is not carried only by fat-only cells.

scenes.tts: Remove sodium glucose transporter one, and gut sugar responses disappear while fat responses remain. Remove combinations of fat receptors, and fat responses fall. The inputs can separate.
scenes.caption: Remove SGLT1, and gut sugar responses disappear while fat responses remain. Remove combinations of fat receptors, and fat responses fall. The inputs can separate.
scenes.visual: Show a two-row response board. Row 1, 'SGLT1 absent': sugar lamp changes GREEN to RED-off; fat lamp stays GREEN. Row 2, 'fat-receptor combinations absent': sugar lamp stays neutral; fat lamp falls RED. Reset lamps before each row. No gene or receptor structures are drawn.
scenes.narration: Remove SGLT1, and gut sugar responses disappear while fat responses remain. Remove combinations of fat receptors, and fat responses fall. The inputs can separate.

scenes.tts: Here is the guiding idea in action. Match each claim to its link: epithelial sensor, vagal response, brainstem learning, or behaviour. Do not merge their timescales.
scenes.visual: The world stretches into four large connected stations filling the frame: GOLD 'epithelial sensor', BLUE 'vagal response', WHITE 'brainstem learning', GREEN 'behaviour'. A pulse moves across them while separate clocks appear below: milliseconds, seconds, and hours, all labelled 'different measurements'.
scenes.narration: Here is the guiding idea in action. Match each claim to its link: epithelial sensor, vagal response, brainstem learning, or behaviour. Do not merge their timescales.

scenes.tts: These are mouse circuits. Germline deletions do not identify the required cell type. Silencing labelled populations is acute but not perfectly pure. Human behaviour remains untested here.
scenes.visual: A boundary labelled 'mouse evidence' encloses the four stations. Under it, two caution cards slide in: 'germline deletion: whole animal' and 'labelled population: not perfectly pure'. A human silhouette remains outside the boundary with label 'behaviour not tested here'.
scenes.narration: These are mouse circuits. Germline deletions do not identify the required cell type. Silencing labelled populations is acute but not perfectly pure. Human behaviour remains untested here.

scenes.tts: The moving picture leaves exact genotypes, sample sizes and the preference calculation to the text. It also leaves a harder naming problem: three different G L P one routes.
scenes.caption: The moving picture leaves exact genotypes, sample sizes and the preference calculation to the text. It also leaves a harder naming problem: three different GLP-1 routes.
scenes.visual: The four stations shrink upward. Three empty parallel lanes rise below them, each labelled only 'GLP-1?' with separate question marks. A downward arrow points to text: 'Exact evidence and three routes below'.
scenes.narration: The moving picture leaves exact genotypes, sample sizes and the preference calculation to the text. It also leaves a harder naming problem: three different GLP-1 routes.

scenes.visual: End card over the dim gut-to-vagus world. Large centred line: 'In mice, the gut teaches preference through separable sensory routes.' GOLD and WHITE nutrient symbols drift into separate BLUE branches behind the text.
